|  | This document concerns requirements for enabling components from customers either explicitly (i.e. requests coming directly from Intel’s customers) or implicitly (i.e. requirements that are based on industry capability such as SMT or reflow requirements).  Both types of requirements are included.  Other important distinctions are as follows.   In Scope: Mechanical, thermal, and manufacturing related ingredients for the design and manufacture of products which are sold by Intel’s customers. This includes products manufactured by Intel and Enabled Components as defined below. An Enabled component is a component not sold by Intel and is necessary for the proper function of the platform.  Enabled components are categorized into the following groups. • Thermal solution (processor and power delivery and includes TIM2)  • Socket  • Retention (e.g., back plate, spring, standoffs, etc.)  • Tools, jigs, fixtures, etc. required for assembly / disassembly, measurements  Out of scope:  • Requirements for debug and probing tools  • Requirements for Test tools (thermal test tools, etc.)  • Power delivery (e.g. VR heatsinks, Voltage Regulator Test Tool) |  |  |  |  | 12 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | |  | Load Mechanism: Heatsink Attach | 1.  LM allows for flat-bottom heatsink 2.  Pedestals (if needed) must allow for adequate thermal solutions.  3.  LM must allow heatsink to be selected by customer (customers have flexibility in heatsink design).  4.  Retention design must accommodate both a traditional air cooled heat sink and a liquid cooled, cold plate based thermal solution (LAAC, liquid cooling, etc.) 5.  Retention must allow for flexible and rigid tubing to route in/out of the thermal solution volumetric from both the front and rear ends (for heat pipes, liquid cooling, etc).  Routing in/out the sides is desireable as well, but lower in priority.  Specific tubing sizes and quantities TBD. 6.  Custom thermal solutions must be able to grow beyond the sides of the enabled thermal solution volume.  Front and rear growth is beneficial to have.  (Much more customer benefit in being able to growth width than length, but length is still helpful.) 7.  Enabling drawings shall include a thermal solution agnostic Interface Control Drawing indicating features needed for for a thermal solution to work with the enabled retention soluion, and which may be used for development of non-reference thermal solutions of various types. Replaceable heatsinks must either be obviously keyed for only the correct orientation, or they must be symmetrical. Keying must have at least 10mm difference in locations of mechanical features which provide the keying. (for visual reference) 3. |  | On Package Cable / Connector Insertion and Removal Features | 1.  Pre-kit (or on "PHM") needed – must minimize assembly action inside of chassis.  2.  Must be viable on both cell and continuous flow manufacturing lines and meet Intel Ergo Guidelines 3.  Detection mechanism required to assure correct orientation and electrical connections.  • Loading mechanism must not engage if misaligned.  • Robust blind mate (alignment guides to prevent misalignment). IIntuitive assembly (i.e. universal markings, color blindness capability, no instruction manual mindset) • Ensure that connectors, CPU or similar components provide clear audible or tactile feedback (e.g., a noticeable "click" or a change in resistance) when they are correctly fitted into place  • Ability to visually confirm On Package connects to Processor. This may be insertion mark, presence pin  • Electrical confirmation  • Connector feature needed to prevent inadvertent disconnect  4.  Post sales On Package Cable / Connector adds must be supported. Must allow for On Package Cable / Connector replacement without disturbing CPU   5.  All user-operable handles, latches, levers, and touch points must be made with sufficient robustness to ensure they will not break or cause damage during customer and servicer usage. No added defect level. No risk of customer cable pull causing undetectable fail   6. |  | On Package Cable / Connector Cable Management | 1.  Solution must prevent damage to the On Package Cable / Connector including contact with adjacent heatsinks. Assembly / disassembly interference from "dangling" On Package Cable / Connector cables and system must be prevented  2.  Solution must work with stacked risers and allow for rework / replace / upgrade of nested risers. Cables must not prevent access to other components (i.e., they must not "trap" parts) 3.  Must be capable of folds (creases) to assist with cable routability. Minimum distance is half cable width to enable 180 degree turn). Clip to board recommendations needed.  4. |  | Package Carrier (NEW) | -  Package carrier shall provide robust retention of CPU while assembled. -  Carrier shall have a robust keying feature that allows a custom thermal solution to optionally install in only one orientation relative to the carrier.  -  If feasible, carrier should allow the reference thermal solution to install in either of 2 orientations (rotated 180deg from each other, as on Purley reference HS and package carrier). | Purley / Groveport Customer Feedback | -  Purley package carrier seemed compliant and did not feel robust/secure to some customers. -  Vertical pin on (6.4 kg) must have a camming lever to give the user a mechanical advantage, thus reducing the force required by the user to less than 14 lb. (6.4 kg). |  | This document concerns requirements for enabling components from customers either explicitly (i.e. requests coming directly from Intel’s customers) or implicitly (i.e. requirements that are based on industry capability such as SMT or reflow requirements).  Both types of requirements are included.  Other important distinctions are as follows.   In Scope: Mechanical, thermal, and manufacturing related ingredients for the design and manufacture of products which are sold by Intel’s customers. This includes products manufactured by Intel and Enabled Components as defined below. An Enabled component is a component not sold by Intel and is necessary for the proper function of the platform.  Enabled components are categorized into the following groups. • Thermal solution (processor and power delivery and includes TIM2)  • Socket  • Retention (e.g., back plate, spring, standoffs, etc.)  • Tools, jigs, fixtures, etc. required for assembly / disassembly, measurements  Out of scope:  • Requirements for debug and probing tools  • Requirements for Test tools (thermal test tools, etc.)  • |  | Other Key System Information | ODM * Installation and removals includes bench rework operations (may occur multiple times- assumption is up to 10) * All will remove covers at functional test; Dell has need to remove covers at ict. Some test operations automated * WS shipped as L10,  other servers are not shipped with MB installed in chassis – Dell * Ship from ODM may include populated socket, unpopulated socket, heatsink only in socket System HVM * No pre-kitting today (processor thrown into box)…recently looked at prekitting for cpu install, but ended nixed. Not impossible though) * Blade is continuous line, rack and towers are cell builds * May be kitted or assembled into chassis * Ship to field may include populated socket, unpopulated socket, heatsink only in socket Field * Removal should include 1U to 5U  (sub 1U blades, small as possible) * Brick disassembly in field needs to be possible *  repair in rack, no workbench, built up in the system * Servicing much be achieved with DIMMs installed (field) * In field, the socket cover is removed on new board and put onto board to be returned.  * Field Scenarios - replace board only, heatsink only (esp fanned HS); processor reuse, processor swap; Boxed processors used in field (suggest option kit for PHM). Field replace-ability includes placing a new motherboard with existing CPU - Accessibility and damage protection process needs to be defined * Assume heatsink solution to support upgrades (Platforms may start with EP...upgrade to EX, On-connect added in field) -  * Training - 30% turnover for field service (web based training) - also used end customer install (no training); Starting with Romley - customer may do the replace if desired. FRU * Full brick as FRU will have manufacturing test (thermal impact - "heated and glued"). FRUs on shelf is 7 years - IBM * No pre-kitting in field. |  | Load Mechanism: Heatsink Attach | 1.  LM allows for flat-bottom heatsink 2.  Pedestals (if needed) must allow for adequate thermal solutions.  3.  LM must allow heatsink to be selected by customer (customers have flexibility in heatsink design).  4.  Retention design must accommodate both a traditional air cooled heat sink and a liquid cooled, cold plate based thermal solution (LAAC, liquid cooling, etc.) 5.  Retention must allow for flexible and rigid tubing to route in/out of the thermal solution volumetric from both the front and rear ends (for heat pipes, liquid cooling, etc).  Routing in/out the sides is desireable as well, but lower in priority.  Specific tubing sizes and quantities TBD. 6.  Custom thermal solutions must be able to grow beyond the sides of the enabled thermal solution volume.  Front and rear growth is beneficial to have.  (Much more customer benefit in being able to growth width than length, but length is still helpful.) 7.  Enabling drawings shall include a thermal solution agnostic Interface Control Drawing indicating features needed for for a thermal solution to work with the enabled retention soluion, and which may be used for development of non-reference thermal solutions of various types.  (e.g. a customer's customer liquid cooling cold plate or passive air heat sink) | Legacy, Purley and Groveport |  | T/M Design Team | 104 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | Actuation mechanism and its housing shall be designed such that motion is obstacle free in its actuation direction, but limited in its unactuated position.  3.    The load must not close when incorrectly oriented. LM must be keyed to socket   4.  PHM actuation is error free (captive screws, screws or actuation at appropriate height to prevent damage, no torque sequencing or errors due to tilted screws). |  | Heatsink Chassis Attach | 1. Heatsink retention  shall not require direct chassis attach  2. Replaceable heatsinks must either be obviously keyed for only the correct orientation, or they must be symmetrical. Keying must have at least 10mm difference in locations of mechanical features which provide the keying. (for visual reference) 3. Heatsink fasteners should use  • #2 Phillips head  • less than 10 in-lb torque  • Captive fasteners  • Cupped head to prevent driver from slipping off  • Fasteners must not be 4-40 thread or smaller |  | On Package Cable / Connector Insertion and Removal Features | 1.  Pre-kit (or on "PHM") needed – must minimize assembly action inside of chassis.  2.  Must be viable on both cell and continuous flow manufacturing lines and meet Intel Ergo Guidelines 3.  Detection mechanism required to assure correct orientation and electrical connections.  • Loading mechanism must not engage if misaligned.  • Robust blind mate (alignment guides to prevent misalignment). IIntuitive assembly (i.e. universal markings, color blindness capability, no instruction manual mindset) • Ensure that connectors, CPU or similar components provide clear audible or tactile feedback (e.g., a noticeable "click" or a change in resistance) when they are correctly fitted into place  • Ability to visually confirm On Package connects to Processor. This may be insertion mark, presence pin  • Electrical confirmation  • Connector feature needed to prevent inadvertent disconnect  4.  Post sales On Package Cable / Connector adds must be supported. Must allow for On Package Cable / Connector replacement without disturbing CPU   5.  All user-operable handles, latches, levers, and touch points must be made with sufficient robustness to ensure they will not break or cause damage during customer and servicer usage. |  | On Package Cable / Connector Cable Management | 1.  Solution must prevent damage to the On Package Cable / Connector including contact with adjacent heatsinks. Assembly / disassembly interference from "dangling" On Package Cable / Connector cables and system must be prevented  2.  Solution must work with stacked risers and allow for rework / replace / upgrade of nested risers. Cables must not prevent access to other components (i.e., they must not "trap" parts) 3.  Must be capable of folds (creases) to assist with cable routability. Minimum distance is half cable width to enable 180 degree turn). Clip to board recommendations needed.  4. |  | Package Carrier (NEW) | -  Package carrier shall provide robust retention of CPU while assembled. -  Carrier shall have a robust keying feature that allows a custom thermal solution to optionally install in only one orientation relative to the carrier.  -  If feasible, carrier should allow the reference thermal solution to install in either of 2 orientations (rotated 180deg from each other, as on Purley reference HS and package carrier). | Purley / Groveport Customer Feedback | -  Purley package carrier seemed compliant and did not feel robust/secure to some customers. -  Vertical pin on Purley carrier was a visual indicator that was too weak to serve as a key; however, there was customer interest in using it as a key for thermal solutions that needed to install in only one |  | Ergo Features – for alignment and keying | 1. When alignment features are utilized in a component that is slid into a socket or connector the key interference must be encountered in the first 25% of the install travel of the component. This is mostly used for large components such as heat sinks that have large installation travel distance  2. When keying is utilized in a component that is slid into a socket or connector the key should be visible to the installer.  3.
